review.decision: Exercise the observed collision and independent recovery before broader monitoring changes
review.notes: Synthetic HOME, fake clock, fake pane and fake native driver only. The resident and original queue remain outside the test boundary. Independent review takes place on the exact candidate.

cases.description: Exact legacy collision isolates only the affected wake
cases.setup: Make two distinct, privately owned legacy incarnations under the same keyed physical name. Persist authentic v2 intent and pin evidence for both; park the first and leave the second sending. Add an unrelated due wake. Include a malformed recovery record as a separately checked whole-channel failure.
cases.action: Drain twice with an isolated native fake after the persisted state is created.
cases.expected: Both original inodes, bytes, pins and journal records remain. The independent wake submits exactly once without paste or replay. Unreadable or unidentifiable intent still prevents all admission.

cases.description: Keyed merge preserves pending identity and new incarnations never reuse it
cases.setup: Fake fixed clock with the same due time over several attempts, an existing pre-upgrade keyed entry, and a positive native busy refusal while a producer posts an update.
cases.action: Replace the queued legacy payload, claim it, and enqueue two further payloads, including a same-key update during the refusal seam.
cases.expected: An unclaimed merge keeps its due time and identity. A new generation has a distinct name even at identical due time. It cannot overwrite an existing sending or parked entry. A provably refused obsolete generation yields to a newer pending one while uncertain records remain frozen. Neither operation pastes into the pane.
